caption_first_line: He spent $3,000 on pudding he never ate. Best deal of his life.
caption_body: In 1999 a civil engineer spotted a frequent flyer promotion on pudding cups and did the math nobody else did. The result: over a million airline miles from a garage full of dessert.
keywords_line: frequent flyer miles hack · pudding guy · airline miles loophole · travel hacking story
comment_question: Would you have bought twelve thousand puddings? Be honest.
pinned_comment: Sources: Snopes 'Pudding on the Ritz', CNN transcript (Jan 2000), UC Davis News, Wikipedia: David Phillips. Why didn't he just order online? It was 1999: he had to find it store by store. Case #002 next: the lifetime ticket an airline regretted.
trial_variants: A man filled his garage with twelve thousand puddings, and an airline paid for it.
Pudding was the cheapest airline ticket in America, and only one man noticed.
yt_title: The Pudding That Paid for Free Flights
yt_description: In 1999 an engineer turned $3,000 of pudding into 1.25 million airline miles. Sources in the pinned comment.
